en: May the son of the Sun, clad in blue garments, with a dark-blue body, wearing a crown, seated upon a vulture, wielding a bow, and inspiring awe—may he, four-armed, gracious, and tranquil, ever be the bestower of boons upon me. (1)
Brahmā said: Listen, all you sages, to this great and unsurpassed armor of the Sun’s son, the king Śani, which removes the affliction caused by Śani. 2.
This armor, the abode of deities known as the "Vajra Cage," brings delight to Śanaiścara and bestows all auspicious fortune. ||3||
Oṃ! May Śanaiścara protect my head; may the son of the Sun protect my forehead. May the son of Chāyā protect my eyes, and may the younger brother of Yama protect my ears. (4)
May Vaivasvata protect my nose, and may Bhāskara always protect my face; may Snigdhakaṇṭha protect my throat, and may Mahābhuja protect my two arms.
May Śani protect the shoulders, and may the bestower of auspiciousness protect the hands;
may the brother of Yama protect the chest, and likewise may Asita protect the belly.
May the Lord of Planets protect my navel; may Manda likewise protect my waist; may Antaka protect my thighs, and Yama protect the pair of my knees. ||7||
May he who moves with slow gait protect my feet; may Pippala protect my entire body;
and may the son of the Sun protect all my limbs and minor members. (8)
Whoever recites this divine armor-mantra of the son of the Sun shall suffer no affliction, and the Son of the Sun shall be pleased with him. 9.
the second, or the eighth house, or even located in the seventh house, Saturn is always well-pleased.
If Saturn is situated in the eighth house, or in the twelfth house from the natal ascendant,
one who constantly recites this armor-mantra (kavaca) shall never experience suffering anywhere.

This divine armor of the Sun, which was fashioned in ancient times, always destroys the defects arising from the twelfth and eighth houses of birth; the Lord destroys all defects situated in the birth-ascendant. 12.
Thus ends the Śanivajrapañjara-kavaca in the dialogue between Brahmā and Nārada within the glorious Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa.
